cover_letter.name: Earnin cover letter
body_paragraphs: Earnin's app is the place where members decide, often in a hurry, how to handle money between paychecks. The CoreUX role puts one team in charge of that whole experience, from the first screen to the system underneath it. I have spent eight years on consumer apps where trust and clarity matter as much as conversion, and this role fits that.

At Tidewell I led a budgeting app for 3M users. A redesigned bank-linking flow cut sign-up drop-off by 28%, and round-up savings grew monthly active savers by 47%. At Brightpath I rebuilt onboarding around a personalised first session, which lifted day-7 retention from 31% to 39%, and my squad runs more than 60 A/B tests a year.

I have not owned a design system or an ML-driven home screen, and I would be learning that part with your designers and engineers. I would welcome the chance to talk about where the app experience is weakest today and what the team wants to fix first. I am based in Seattle and can work with the Mountain View team two days a week in the office.

autofill.why do you want to work at earnin?: I want to work on a financial product where the app experience directly affects whether someone gets through a tight week. At Tidewell I cut bank-linking drop-off by 28% for a budgeting app, and I saw how much clarity and trust matter in money products. Earnin's CoreUX scope, from home screen to design quality, is a chance to own that end to end.
autofill.describe a time you used data to make a: A Brightpath paywall test won on trial starts but lost on week-4 retention. I re-cut the results by cohort, argued we should judge on retained revenue rather than starts, and we shipped the variant that lost on trials. It won on revenue by 6%, and the team adopted retained revenue as the default readout.
autofill.how do you balance design quality with g: I treat them as the same goal measured over different time spans. At Brightpath the onboarding rebuild started from user interviews and a design review, then went to an experiment. Day-7 retention rose from 31% to 39%, so the more considered first session also paid off in the numbers. I pair with design from the first spec.
autofill._default: I enjoy owning a consumer experience end to end: research, experiments and shipping with a small cross-functional team. This role is close to my work on onboarding, bank linking and retention at Brightpath and Tidewell, and I would be glad to talk through the details.

cover_letter.name: Mudflap cover letter
body_paragraphs: A driver who signs up for a fuel card is trying to save money at the pump today, not read a tutorial. Getting that person from sign-up to a first discounted fill is the growth problem in this role, and it is the kind of problem I like: a short path, a clear metric and a lot of room to test.

At Brightpath I rebuilt onboarding and moved day-7 retention from 31% to 39%, and paywall tests I ran added $9M in recurring revenue. At Tidewell I cut drop-off in a bank-linking flow by 28% with a redesign and in-app education. My squad runs over 60 A/B tests a year, and I read the funnels and cohorts myself in SQL.

I have not worked in trucking, so I would start by riding along with drivers and fleet operators and talking to them directly, as I did with shoppers and savers in past roles. I would welcome a conversation about where onboarding loses people today and which fixes the team has already tried. I am based in Seattle and comfortable with the Palo Alto office.

autofill.why do you want to work at mudflap?: Mudflap sells a payment product to people who count every dollar, which makes growth work honest: if onboarding is confusing, drivers leave. I have done that kind of work in consumer fintech at Tidewell and in subscriptions at Brightpath. I want to apply it to a market I do not know yet and learn it by talking to drivers and fleet operators.
autofill.describe a time you improved activation: At Brightpath, new users were dropping before finishing a first session. I ran interviews, then rebuilt onboarding around a personalised first session and tested it against the old flow. Day-7 retention rose from 31% to 39% and trial starts rose by 22%. We kept the test running for four weeks to confirm retention held.
autofill.how do you use ai tools in your work?: I use AI assistants to summarise interview notes, draft first versions of PRDs and write SQL that I then check by hand. It shortens the path from a question to a query. I am also interested in where AI could help inside a product, such as guiding setup, but I would test that with users before committing to it.
autofill._default: I like owning growth for a consumer product: onboarding, activation and the experiments that prove what works. This role matches my work at Brightpath and Tidewell, and I would be glad to talk through the details and learn how Mudflap's customers use the product.

body_paragraphs: Link is the first moment a person trusts an app with their bank account, and a small change in how many people finish it has a large effect downstream. That is why the Link Growth role stands out to me. I have spent several years on exactly that step, from the consumer side, watching where people hesitate, where a bank connection fails and what it takes to bring them back.

At Tidewell I led bank linking for a budgeting app with 3M users and six aggregator integrations. Moving to a provider-agnostic API layer raised link success from 81% to 93%, and a redesigned flow with in-app education cut sign-up drop-off by 28%. I worked with security and legal on consent and data retention, and at Brightpath I built the experiment toolkit our squads use.

I have not yet worked on agent-based use cases, and I would like to learn how Link needs to change for them. I would welcome a conversation about where conversion is lowest today, how the team measures it and which experiments are queued next. I am based in Seattle and open to regular time in the San Francisco office.

autofill.why do you want to work at plaid?: Link is the step I know best. At Tidewell I owned bank linking for a consumer app, and I watched a few points of conversion decide whether a user ever saw value. Plaid owns that step for much of the industry. I want to work on conversion at that scale and learn how Link has to change as more AI-driven products use it.
autofill.describe a time you improved a conversio: At Tidewell, many users dropped between sign-up and linking their first account. We moved to a provider-agnostic aggregation layer so users fell back to a second provider when one failed, and redesigned the flow with in-app education. Link success rose from 81% to 93%, and sign-up to first-linked-account drop-off fell by 28%.
autofill.how do you work with legal and complianc: I bring them in at the spec stage rather than at launch. At Tidewell I worked with security and legal on consent screens, data retention rules and the SOC 2 evidence for consumer financial data. Early involvement meant fewer late changes, and we shipped the linking flow without reopening those decisions.
autofill._default: I like owning a conversion metric that sits at the front door of a product. This role matches my work on bank linking at Tidewell and experimentation tooling at Brightpath, and I would be glad to talk through the details.

cover_letter.name: Ramp cover letter
body_paragraphs: Ramp's growth work sits on top of billing, data and trust, and that is the territory I know best. I should say plainly that my eight years have been on consumer apps rather than B2B finance tools, so I would be learning your customers. I am applying because the combination of experiments and financial data is where my work has been strongest.

At Brightpath I replaced a legacy billing integration with a unified subscription service, cutting failed renewals by 18% and recovering $2.4M, and I built the experiment toolkit our squads use. At Tidewell I moved bank data to a provider-agnostic layer, lifted link success from 81% to 93%, and worked with security and legal on consent and SOC 2 evidence. I write my own SQL.

I do not have partner-channel experience or a track record of AI prototyping to point to yet, and I would be building both from a lower base than your ideal candidate. If that is still of interest, I would welcome a conversation. I am based in Seattle and can work from the New York or San Francisco office.

autofill.why do you want to work at ramp?: Ramp builds software around money movement, where accuracy and trust decide whether customers stay. I have worked on that kind of product on the consumer side: billing and subscriptions at Brightpath and bank data at Tidewell. I want to apply the same experiment-driven habits to a B2B product, and I know I would need to learn finance teams' workflows first.
autofill.describe a time you used data to make a: At Brightpath, failed renewals were hurting subscription revenue and the cause was unclear. I pulled the billing data in SQL, found a pattern in retries on one legacy integration, and proposed replacing it with a unified subscription service. Failed renewals fell by 18% and we recovered $2.4M.
autofill.how do you handle sensitive financial da: I bring security and legal in early. At Tidewell I worked with them on consent screens, data retention and the evidence needed for SOC 2, before we built anything on top of the bank data. I also keep the user informed about what is shared and give them a clear way to revoke it.
autofill._default: I enjoy product work where data, experiments and trust meet, which is how I would describe billing and bank-data platforms. I have done this for consumer apps at Brightpath and Tidewell, and I would like to learn the B2B side at Ramp. I am happy to talk through the details.
